about.title: About Dahab Hostel — Family Run in Downtown Cairo Since 1998
about.subtitle: Started in 1998 on a Downtown Cairo rooftop, now run by the second generation. Nearly 30 years and over 800,000 guests from all over the world.
paragraphs: Dahab hostel was founded in 1998. This family run business has been registered in all the major guidebooks and travel websites where it has consistently received positive reviews.

It all started when Dr. Abdel Alim El Tamamy, a general surgeon, visited a friend of his that was living in the same building. The apartments of the colonial downtown building had their storage rooms on top of the roof. That was when the idea was born.

We love to travel. We love Dahab. The love of travel and especially in Sinai made us choose the name Dahab, after the beach town. The hostel is a recreation of a laid-back beach camp in the heart of the capital. It's like a little oasis in the city!

Over the years we were blessed to have the kindest people working with us helping us grow the business and our big community, our family. Our returning guests will confirm: Dahab hostel has something magical!
about.quote: I have a crazy idea, we could turn this place into a hostel
about.quoteBy: Now we run Dahab hostel in the second generation.

location.title: Dahab Hostel Location — Downtown Cairo
location.subtitle: We are centrally located on Mahmoud Bassiouny Street at Talaat Harb Square, minutes from the Egyptian Museum and the metro.
location.intro: Dahab hostel is centrally located in the heart of Downtown Cairo. It is just a 3-minute walking distance to the Egyptian Museum, and within easy reach of the main train and bus stations by public transportation, taxi or Metro.
directions: From Abdel Menem Ryad Square, take the road to Mahmoud Bassiouny Street
From Talaat Harb Square, take the road to Mahmoud Bassiouny Street (Groppi on the corner)
location.taxi: Transportation in Cairo is affordable and safe. Most taxis will know how to get to Dahab hostel when you give them the address. White taxis have a meter but remember to carry the right amount of change.
location.metro: The metro is fast and cheap. Drop off at Sadat Station (Tahrir Sq.), the hostel is a 5-minute walk via Talaat Harb Street to Talaat Harb Square and then Mahmoud Bassiouny Street.
location.pickup: You will find our representative waiting for you holding a sign of your name and Dahab hostel, after passport control and customs clearance.
location.pickupPrice: From 1 to 3 PaX, from 550 EGP per car. For groups of more than 3 PaX, contact us for a quote.

cityInfo.title: Cairo Travel Tips — Getting Around, Taxis, Metro and Money
cityInfo.subtitle: Practical advice on getting around Cairo, taxis, the metro, money and staying safe, from a hostel that has welcomed guests here since 1998.

sections.title: Visas
sections.text: Non-Egyptian visitors arriving in Egypt are required to have a valid passport. Most tourists can obtain an entry visa at any of the major entry ports for $25.00.

sections.title: Passport
sections.text: Your passport will be collected at our hostel upon arrival. The staff retain a copy of your passport details as a standard check-in procedure.

sections.title: Food and Water
sections.text: Drink only bottled water, available at the hostel. In the first few days eat lightly and avoid raw vegetables or fruits unless you can peel them.

sections.title: Medical Assistance
sections.text: Medical assistance is available throughout Egypt. Speak with the front desk manager for help locating a physician or medical center.

sections.title: Money
sections.text: The local currency is the Egyptian Pound (EGP), divided into 100 piasters. ATMs are plentiful in Cairo and accept a wide variety of credit cards.

sections.title: Tipping
sections.text: Tips or Baksheesh are an integral part of Egyptian culture. Keep a stack of small bills handy for tips; no change is given.

sections.title: Scams and Touts
sections.text: Be polite but firm; say 'la Shukran' (no thank you) to persistent touts. They are harmless but can test your good manners.

sections.title: Taxis
sections.text: Taxis are very affordable and safe. Carry the right amount of change to avoid being taken.

sections.title: Clothing
sections.text: Egypt is a casual country. Day dress should include cotton, breathable fabrics, comfortable shoes, hat and sunglasses.
